info.name: Iotku V2 WebSocket
info.description: Minimal WebSocket-only collection for Iotku V2. Import this collection and the `Iotku V2 WebSocket Local` environment. If your Postman version imports these as normal GET requests, create a new WebSocket request manually and copy the URL/message examples from each request description.

request.description:
Open this URL as a WebSocket request.

Send raw message:

```text
27.5
```

Expected behavior: backend stores a sensor reading for `{{sensor_code}}` and broadcasts the update to clients in the same sensor room.

Open this URL as a WebSocket request.

Send JSON message:

```json
{
  "value": "27.5",
  "recorded_at_ms": 1760000000000
}
```

You can also use legacy field names:

```json
{
  "nilai": "27.5",
  "waktu": 1760000000000
}
```

Open this URL as a WebSocket request.

Send JSON message:

```json
{
  "type": "device_info"
}
```

Expected behavior: backend responds with connection status, IP device, and connected timestamp.

Open this URL as a WebSocket request.

Send admin handshake:

```json
{
  "isAdmin": true,
  "key": "{{ws_admin_key}}"
}
```

`ws_admin_key` must match `WS_ADMIN_KEY` in backend `.env`.

Expected behavior: backend responds with connected clients and sensor rooms. New sensor events are also sent to this admin socket.
